nodes.answer: The four potential interaction roles identified are informing, stimulating, simulating, and mediating.
nodes.paragraph: BSalla Jarske salla.jarske@tuni. 1Faculty of Information Technology and CommunicationSciences, Tampere University, Tampere, FinlandIn this paper, we use the term young people to refer primarily to people transitioning from childhood to adult- hood, within the age range of 15 24 years [ 4]. Young people are unique in that they are gradually acquiring equal rightsand responsibilities to participate in society in the sameway adults do (e.g., voting rights, employment, managing nances) [ 5]. They also face unique generational issues such as globalization, climate change [ 6], and different political ideologies or disputes. Many young people are concerned about societal issues but encounter structural barriers, such as voting age or lack of opportunities, as well as psychologicalbarriers, such as disinterest or distrust in participation pro- cesses, or they lack the necessary skills to participate and take action [ 7 9]. Increasingly, young people are turning to digital forms of participation [ 10]. Barriers in digital environments seem to be lower for young people than in more traditional forms of participation, and digital technologies can offer engaging ways for youth to express their views on societalissues and take part in social movements [ 9].

nodes.question: What are the four potential interaction roles identified for robots supporting societal participation according to the findings from the workshops?
nodes.answer: The four potential interaction roles for robots supporting societal participation are informing, stimulating, simulating, and mediating.
nodes.paragraph: Our research approach is Research through Design, in which artefacts are designed and subsequently analyzed to identify opportuni-ties for technology utilization and to re ect on their potentialimpacts on the world [ 28]. For this study, we collected data from ve exploratory design workshops with high school and university students, as engaging youth in the design of tech-nologies allows them to voice their perspectives [ 3,29]. The purpose of the workshops was to generate ideas and con- cepts regarding robot-supported or robot-mediated societalparticipation. The research question for this paper is: Whatforms of societal participation are addressed in social robot concepts designed by young people? The contributions of this study include a variety of social robot concepts, which provide a deeper understanding of the potential uses of social robots to support societal participationof youth, and four possible interaction roles for civic robots. These ndings can serve as inspiration and a framework for further exploration in the research and design of robots for societal participation, extending beyond the youth age group. nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How does the term "interactive governance" relate to civil society and the business sector?
nodes.answer: Interactive governance expresses the interaction between various initiatives, organizations, and movements of civil society, as well as advocates from the business sector.
nodes.paragraph: When the term interactive governance is preferred in the following, this does not mean to adopt one special string in the governance debate. It is rather chosen because this term expresses particularly well a central challenge forgovernance in the liberal democracies of today: to nd and re-form institutionalised forms of interplay and interme- diation between the side of political representatives andadministrators on the one hand and the spheres of society on the other hand. These forms reach from the various initiatives, organisations, and movements of a civil societyover to the advocates of the business sector. Interactive Governance in a Democracy The idea of interactive governance is closely linked to questions of appreciating, using, and revitalising theopportunities which can be provided by a liberal demo- cratic order. The question is: how can traditional repre- sentative and new participative forms of politics and1 14 Voluntas (2025) 36:113 124 123 governance be combined? To what extent are the new ones likely to in uence or even displace the old ones? Will combinations of traditional and new elements enable more democracy, possibilities for dealing with the future, landsecuring citizens rights?

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What types of online platforms are mentioned as places for individuals to exchange opinions and concerns?
nodes.answer: The online platforms mentioned include Twitter (now known as X), Instagram, Facebook, and other specialized online forums.
nodes.paragraph: As digital technology advances, numerous online platforms such as Twitter (officially known now as X), Instagram, Facebook and other specialised online forums have emerged, which serve as a virtual space for individuals to exchange their opinions, perspec- tives, and concerns, and they are becoming increas- ingly popular and influential in providing a real-time record of public sentiment (Arlt et al., 2018; Fronzetti Colladon, 2018). Research on such social media con- tent can offer a deeper understanding of the social perception, social contexts of specific policies, and potential solutions to bridge existing gaps (Li et al., 2019). Fronzetti Colladon, (2018) highlights that spontaneous consumer expressions can provide valua- ble insights into product features and user experience when analysed without creating a sense of surveil- lance. In this context, user-generated reviews on app- provision platforms such as Google Play Store and Apple App Store offer a useful means of understand- ing users perceptions and feedback on the apps they use (Cambria et al., 2016). These reviews serve as a valuable source of information, and systematically analysing the vast amount of user-generated content can help reveal evolving attitudes towards smart solu- tions, particularly in relation to household energy use (Genc-Nayebi & Abran, 2017; Mariani & Borghi, 2022).
